sentences.en: From The New York Times, this is The Interview.
sentences.zh: 这里是《纽约时报》出品的《访谈》栏目。

sentences.en: I'm David Marchese.
sentences.zh: 我是大卫·马尔凯塞。

sentences.en: The arrival of Sally Rooney's new novel Intermezzo this month is absolutely one of the fall's biggest publishing events.
sentences.zh: 萨利·鲁尼本月推出的新小说《间奏曲》绝对是今秋最大的出版盛事之一。

sentences.en: Not only for all the readers hungry for new fiction from the 33-year-old Irish author, and that includes myself, but for all the book lovers, again, myself included,
sentences.zh: 不仅对于所有渴望这位33岁爱尔兰作家创作的新小说的读者来说——这其中也包括我，而且对于所有书迷来说——同样包括我自己，

sentences.en: eager for the flood of think pieces and commentary that Intermezzo will surely spawn.
sentences.zh: 他们都急切地等待着《间奏曲》必然会引发的大量评论和深度文章。

sentences.en: Rooney is one of those rare authors who's been able to earn a mass readership as well as serious critical attention.
sentences.zh: 鲁尼是那种罕见的作家，她既能赢得大众读者的青睐，也能获得严肃的文学评论界关注。

sentences.en: Maybe I should just say attention, period.
sentences.zh: 也许我应该直接说，就是关注，句号。

sentences.en: The popular success is, on some level, easier to understand.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，大众的成功更容易理解。

sentences.en: Her four novels are beautifully written relationship studies, someone else might dare call them romances, that weave together politics, sex, moral philosophy, dry humor,
sentences.zh: 她的四部小说都是文笔优美的两性关系研究——别人或许敢称之为言情小说——它们将政治、性、道德哲学、冷幽默，

sentences.en: and a distinctly millennial unease with the state of the world.
sentences.zh: 以及一种对世界现状特有的千禧一代焦虑感交织在一起。

sentences.en: It's a compelling combo, one that found an even broader fan base after her first two novels,
sentences.zh: 这是一个引人入胜的组合，在她的前两部小说《聊天记录》和《正常人》被改编成热门剧集后，它收获了更广泛的粉丝基础。

sentences.en: Conversations with Friends and Normal People, were adapted into buzzy TV series.
sentences.zh: 《聊天记录》和《正常人》。

sentences.en: The lightning rod aspect to Rooney and her work is a little more mysterious.
sentences.zh: 鲁尼及其作品自带的争议性则显得有些神秘。

sentences.en: I'm sure any writer who gets held up like Rooney does as the voice of a generation is sure to be scrutinized.
sentences.zh: 我确信，任何像鲁尼这样被奉为一代人代言人的作家，都注定会受到审视。

sentences.en: But the outsized amount and the intensity of both the praise and the criticism of her output feels a little confusing, including to Rooney, who, as she told me,
sentences.zh: 但对她作品的赞誉和批评，其规模之大、强度之高，却让人感到有些困惑，鲁尼自己也是如此，正如她告诉我的，

sentences.en: would much rather let her work speak for itself.
sentences.zh: 她宁愿让自己的作品不言自明。

sentences.en: And yet, here's my conversation with Sally Rooney.
sentences.zh: 然而，这就是我和萨利·鲁尼的对话。

sentences.en: I was just reading a brief interview you did with The New Yorker that ran in conjunction with an excerpt from Intermezzo.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚读了你为《纽约客》做的一个简短访谈，那是配合《间奏曲》的节选一起发布的。

sentences.en: And I think in there it said that, you said that it's stressful to publish your work and maybe even more stressful to wait for it to be published.
sentences.zh: 我想里面大概提到，你说出版作品压力很大，等待作品出版可能压力更大。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Because I can imagine that like, this is the nice time before you have to worry about how people are actually responding to it or, you know, if it's selling or anything.
sentences.zh: 因为我想象这应该是一段美好的时光，在你不用担心别人实际上会作何反应，或者你知道，它卖得好不好之前。

sentences.en: Now it's like you just got the thing ready to go.
sentences.zh: 现在感觉就像是，你刚把东西准备好推出。

sentences.en: Yeah, but the way that books are published means that actually a lot of the stuff that I find stressful is kind of like front loaded.
sentences.zh: 对，但书的出版方式意味着，实际上我感到压力的很多事情在某种程度上都是提前到来的。

sentences.en: So it happens that, of course, the conversation that we're having right now and the conversations that I'll be having with other journalists
sentences.zh: 所以自然而然地，我们现在正在进行的这段对话，以及我和其他记者将要进行的对话，

sentences.en: about the book will be happening before the book is ever published.
sentences.zh: 关于这本书的对话，都会在这本书出版之前发生。

sentences.en: And that means that the part that involves me, in a sense, putting myself out there and trying to work out a way of talking about my book
sentences.zh: 这意味着涉及我的部分，从某种意义上说，是我把自己置于公众视野中，试图找出一种谈论我书的方式，

sentences.en: happens before the public has had a chance to read it.
sentences.zh: 这发生在公众有机会阅读它之前。

sentences.en: And so it's just a weird mental space to be in.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种很奇妙的心理状态。

sentences.en: I feel like everything that I had to say went into the book and I have nothing left to give that isn't already in the text.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我想表达的一切都写进书里了，除了文本本身，我没有什么可付出的了。

sentences.en: Do you recall if it's ever happened where you've paid attention to the discourse around the book and then had the thought like, oh, I wish I had a chance to respond to that?
sentences.zh: 你还记得是否发生过这样的情况：你关注了围绕这本书的各种言论，然后心里想，哦，我真希望有机会回应那些看法？

sentences.en: I try, and this may sound insincere, but hand on heart, I do actually try not to look at the discourse around my work.
sentences.zh: 我尽量——这听起来可能有点虚伪，但说实话，我真的尽量不去看不关于我作品的讨论。

sentences.en: Of course, some of it filters through and people will just like tell me, you know, things that are being said about my work or whatever.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些声音还是会渗透进来，人们会直接告诉我，你知道的，关于我的作品有哪些议论之类的话。

sentences.en: But I do my best not to look at it too much because I think it would lead me down a bad path.
sentences.zh: 但我尽最大努力不要看太多，因为我认为这会把我引向一条不归路。

sentences.en: And then do I ever feel like responding to it?
sentences.zh: 那我有没有过想回应的冲动？

sentences.en: No, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得没有。

sentences.en: I don't need to be over the reader's shoulder saying,
sentences.zh: 我不需要站在读者的肩膀上说，

sentences.en: Paige, I need to kind of accept that at that point, my work is done, be it good or bad, and let the reader or the critic have their own conversation.
sentences.zh: 佩奇，我需要接受这样一点：在那一刻，我的工作已经完成了，无论好坏，然后让读者或评论家去展开他们自己的对话。

sentences.en: You know, maybe this will be a preview of ways in which people might respond to the new book.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许这会是人们对新书反应方式的一种预演。

sentences.en: But the first question I had about intermezzo is to do with the fact that the two main protagonists, the brothers Ivan and Peter, are obviously guys.
sentences.zh: 但我关于《间奏曲》的第一个问题与这样一个事实有关：两个主要主角，两兄弟伊万和彼得，显然是男性。

sentences.en: And obviously there was Connell and Normal People was a protagonist of that book.
sentences.zh: 显然《正常人》里也有康奈尔作为该书的主角。

sentences.en: But Ivan and Peter really seem central in a way that men haven't been in your books.
sentences.zh: 但伊万和彼得似乎占据了核心地位，这是以往你的书中男性角色所没有的。

sentences.en: And I'm curious if you felt it was a particular challenge to write from a male perspective.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道，你是否觉得从男性的视角来写作是一个特别的挑战？

sentences.en: Yeah, interestingly,
sentences.zh: 是的，有趣的是，

sentences.en: the first voice that came to the page for me in this project was Margaret's voice.
sentences.zh: 在这个项目中，进入我脑海的第一个声音是玛格丽特的。

sentences.en: So the character who becomes entangled in Ivan's life in the course of the book.
sentences.zh: 也就是在书的故事发展中与伊万的生活纠缠在一起的角色。

sentences.en: So it certainly wasn't that I sat down thinking, time to write a book about men.
sentences.zh: 所以绝对不是说我坐下来想，是时候写一本关于男人的书了。

sentences.en: You know, I have to write a book where the male voice is central or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我必须写一本以男性声音为核心的书或者诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: I thought that it was going to be Margaret's story.
sentences.zh: 我本以为这将是玛格丽特的故事。

sentences.en: Of course, I knew that Ivan was a big part of that story.
sentences.zh: 当然，我知道伊万是那个故事的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: But his sort of voice came along rather late in the writing process.
sentences.zh: 但他的声音在写作过程的较晚阶段才出现。

sentences.en: So it definitely was not a conscious project of trying to write about men or trying to write about masculinity.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝不是一个刻意去写男人或刻意去写男性气质的计划。

sentences.en: I just felt my way through the story that seemed to emerge when I encountered these characters.
sentences.zh: 我只是顺着遇到这些角色时自然浮现的故事去感受。

sentences.en: And I kind of followed where they led me, which is what I always tried to do.
sentences.zh: 我顺着他们指引的方向走，这也是我一直以来努力在做的。

sentences.en: Of course, then I had moments of self-reflection and self-consciousness because I was thinking, what, like, do I know, you know, anything about what I'm writing about?
sentences.zh: 当然，后来我也经历过自我反省和自我意识过剩的时刻，因为我在想，什么，比如，我到底知不知道自己在写什么？

sentences.en: But on the other hand, I think, and again, this is from,
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，我认为，再次说明，这来自于，

sentences.en: just having said that I try to ignore all discourse about my work, nonetheless, it has permeated through.
sentences.zh: 刚才我说过我尽量忽略所有关于我作品的讨论，但尽管如此，它们还是渗透了进来。

sentences.en: It filters through that I'm aware that people think that my work is heavily autobiographical.
sentences.zh: 这些议论渗透进来，让我知道人们认为我的作品具有很强的自传性质。

sentences.en: And in fact, it isn't.
sentences.zh: 但实际上并非如此。

sentences.en: So it felt like they were just fictional characters, like all my other fictional characters, and I was intrigued by them.
sentences.zh: 所以感觉他们只是虚构的角色，就像我所有的其他虚构角色一样，我对他们很感兴趣。

sentences.en: I found them really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I liked being with them on the page.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢在书页里和他们待在一起。

sentences.en: And so the question of gender felt very secondary, and it certainly wasn't a conscious theme that I was trying to explore or say something about, as it were.
sentences.zh: 所以性别问题感觉非常次要，它绝对不是一个我刻意想要探讨或借此表达某种看法的刻意主题。

sentences.en: But there were moments where I thought, have I got any of this right?
sentences.zh: 但确实有一些时刻我想过，我有没有把这些写对？

sentences.en: And am I overstepping myself or something?
sentences.zh: 我是不是越界了或者别的什么？

sentences.en: This is not a spoiler or anything, but Peter and Ivan have lost their father.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是剧透，彼得和伊万失去了他们的父亲。

sentences.en: And I was curious about your experience of grief and if, in that instance, you were writing from personal reflection, or if you weren't, did you feel like it was
sentences.zh: 我对你的悲伤体验很感兴趣，在这种情况下，你是基于个人的反思来写作的，还是说，如果不是的话，你会觉得

sentences.en: a particularly difficult task to write into a feeling that deep that you had not experienced?
sentences.zh: 去描绘一种你未曾亲历过的如此深沉的情感是一项极其艰难的任务吗？

sentences.en: I think that's a fair question, but I've never been conscious in writing about any emotional experience that any of my characters have had of drawing on something
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个很合理的问题，但在书写任何角色的情感体验时，我从未有意识地去汲取

sentences.en: that I have felt or known in my own life.
sentences.zh: 我在自己生活中感受过或经历过的东西。

sentences.en: The relationship between fiction and the life of the author is a very live relationship in the minds of readers and critics, and it's a completely
sentences.zh: 虚构作品与作者生活之间的关系，在读者和评论家的脑海中是一个非常活跃的关系，但在我的生活中，它却是一个完全

sentences.en: unknown relationship in my life.
sentences.zh: 未知的关系。

sentences.en: I never, ever think about it.
sentences.zh: 我从来、从来不去想它。

sentences.en: Only when I publish a book do I ever even have to wonder what the relationship between my fiction and my own life is.
sentences.zh: 只有自我出版了一本书之后，我才不得不去琢磨我的虚构作品和我的现实生活之间到底有什么关系。

sentences.en: I sometimes feel that my work is like a little bit like what it might be like to be an actor.
sentences.zh: 我有时觉得我的工作有点像当演员可能会有的体验。

sentences.en: Like, I get very into character and I inhabit that consciousness and that allows me to write about what it is that the character is undergoing.
sentences.zh: 比如，我深深地融入角色，并进入那种意识中，这让我能够写出角色正在经历的事情。

sentences.en: And I'm not in any way saying to myself, well, I know that it would be like this because I remember when something analogous happened to me and I felt like this.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会对自己说，嗯，我知道会是这样，因为我记得当类似的事情发生在我身上时，我是这种感觉。

sentences.en: And I think if I caught myself doing that,
sentences.zh: 我想如果我发现自己这样做，

sentences.en: I'd think there was something wrong with the way that I was working.
sentences.zh: 我会觉得我的工作方式出了问题。

sentences.en: I think at the moment that I found myself reaching for such a thing, I would think there's something,
sentences.zh: 我认为当我发现自己企图借助那种东西时，我会觉得有什么不对劲，

sentences.en: I've lost touch with my character in some way.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上我已经和我的角色失去了联系。

sentences.en: I'm not going to belabor this because there's a lot of other things I want to ask you about, but do you find yourself having thoughts about the writers that are meaningful to you
sentences.zh: 我不想纠缠于此，因为我还有很多其他想问你的问题，但你是否会发现自己去思考那些对你意义重大的作家，

sentences.en: that it seems like people have about you and your work?
sentences.zh: 就像人们对你和你的作品所做的那样？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: You don't?
sentences.zh: 你不会吗？

sentences.en: And curiously...
sentences.zh: 而奇怪的是……

sentences.en: It's like you've never read a biography of a novelist you liked or something like that?
sentences.zh: 这就好像你从来没读过你喜欢的某位小说家的传记一样？

sentences.en: I've actually never read a biography of a writer.
sentences.zh: 我确实从没读过作家的传记。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: I've never.
sentences.zh: 我从来没读过。

sentences.en: And I went...
sentences.zh: 而且我去……

sentences.en: There's some good ones.
sentences.zh: 有些书写得很好。

sentences.en: And people say that there are and I recommended them on a regular basis and I think I must have some kind of mental block to reading them.
sentences.zh: 人们都说有写得很好的，我也经常向别人推荐它们，我想我大脑里一定对阅读它们有一种精神屏障。

sentences.en: Of course there are, let's say, natural gaps in my reading, like I wish there weren't, but I think this is more than a gap.
sentences.zh: 当然，比方说，我的阅读范围里存在一些天然的空白，我希望没有，但我认为这不仅仅是空白。

sentences.en: I think it's like a resistance.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种抵抗。

sentences.en: It's something that is like a stubborn lack of curiosity in me.
sentences.zh: 这就像是我身上一种顽固的缺乏好奇心的表现。

sentences.en: I don't tend to wonder about the relationship between the writer's life and the writer's work.
sentences.zh: 我往往不会去琢磨作家的生活与作家的作品之间的关系。

sentences.en: And, yeah, I think that part of that is...
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，我想其中一部分原因是……

sentences.en: I was going to say part of it might be responsive to a sense that that's an imposed relationship that comes from outside and that I want to resist engaging in that.
sentences.zh: 我本想说，部分原因可能是对某种外界强加的关系的一种抗拒感，我想要拒绝卷入其中。

sentences.en: But I think part of it is a genuine lack of interest because before I ever became a published writer, I also didn't read writers' biographies or even really know anything
sentences.zh: 但我认为部分原因确实是缺乏兴趣，因为在我成为一名出版作家之前，我也不读作家的传记，甚至对作家一无所知。

sentences.en: about writers.
sentences.zh: 关于作家。

sentences.en: I would know what period they lived in, but I would not know anything about...
sentences.zh: 我只知道他们生活在哪个年代，但其他的一概不知……

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's kind of it.
sentences.zh: 对，差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: And I'm still a little bit like that.
sentences.zh: 我到现在还是有点这样。

sentences.en: So I think...
sentences.zh: 所以我想……

sentences.en: And maybe that's why I struggle to answer the kind of questions that you are very reasonably asking because I don't read work in that way.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是为什么我很难回答你那些非常合理的提问，因为我不是以那种方式去阅读作品的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Then do you have...
sentences.zh: 那么你有没有……

sentences.en: Or what might the apprehensions be about sharing your political views?
sentences.zh: 或者说，分享你的政治观点会有什么顾虑吗？

sentences.en: You've written about being against the war in Gaza, for example, or abortion in Ireland, you know.
sentences.zh: 比如，你曾写过反对加沙战争，或者爱尔兰的堕胎问题，你知道的。

sentences.en: So it seems if you're willing to do that, surely you're aware that making your opinions known about these kinds of divisive issues, you know, sort of like opening up
sentences.zh: 所以如果连这些你都愿意去做，那你肯定知道，就这些充满分歧的议题表明你的观点，你知道的，这有点像是在敞开

sentences.en: the possibility that people might conflate
sentences.zh: 这样一种可能性，即人们可能会把

sentences.en: Sally Rooney and your work.
sentences.zh: 萨利·鲁尼本人和你的作品混为一谈。

sentences.en: How do you think about that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么看待这一点的？

sentences.en: Well, that to me feels like a different avenue of conversation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在我看来，这感觉像是对话的另一个方向。

sentences.en: And it's interesting that to you those two things feel quite close and to me they feel quite different.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，对你来说这两件事感觉很接近，而对我来说它们感觉大相径庭。
